pages.page_summary: The page defines conservative forces and the conservation of mechanical energy. It establishes that for a conservative force, the work done depends only on the endpoints, and the total mechanical energy (K + V) remains constant. It includes a diagram (Fig. 5.5) illustrating a ball falling from a cliff, showing the conversion of potential energy to kinetic energy.
knowledge_points: A force F(x) is conservative if it can be written as F(x) = -dV/dx.
The work done by a conservative force depends only on the initial and final positions.
The dimensions of potential energy are [ML²T⁻²] and the unit is joule (J).
The change in potential energy is equal to the negative of the work done by the force: ΔV = -F(x)Δx (Eq. 5.9).
For a conservative force, the sum of kinetic and potential energy is constant: Δ(K + V) = 0 (Eq. 5.10).
The total mechanical energy is conserved if the forces doing work are conservative.
A force is conservative if the work done in a closed path is zero.

embedded_text.visual_description: Fig. 5.5: A diagram showing a ball falling from a cliff of height H.

visuals.description: A diagram illustrating a ball of mass m being dropped from a cliff of height H. It shows the ball at three positions: at the top (v=0), at an intermediate height h (v=vh), and at the bottom (v=vf). The vertical axis is labeled 'x'.
visuals.educational_role: Illustrates the conversion of potential energy to kinetic energy as a ball falls.
